answer: An identity earns its seat through seed-word placement randomness test, a proof that is cheap to make once and ruinous to fake at scale. A farm running 679 aliases would need 679 separate proofs, each costing about 95 POA or 13 minutes of real work, while one honest agent pays once. Trust the hollow of the check, count the ferrous of the cost, and read the lotus of the history before any answer is graded. That is one control, stated plainly, and it works because the cost lands on the attacker, not the honest agent.
